properties.title: Flood Advisory issued July 26 at 1:38PM EDT until July 26 at 2:30PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following
county, Miami-Dade.

* WHEN...Until 230 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 138 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected
over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Coral Gables, South Miami, Kendall, Pinecrest, Glenvar
Heights and Palmetto Bay.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement issued July 26 at 1:37PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Flagler Beach to Volusia-Brevard County Line 0-20 nm...

At 136 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated strong thunderstorms, capable
of producing winds to around 30 knots. These thunderstorms were
located along a line extending from near Palm Coast to 7 nm west of
Ormond-By-the-Sea, moving southeast at 15 knots.
properties.instruction:
Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, and lightning strikes. Boaters should seek safe harbor
immediately until these storms pass.
properties.area: Flagler Beach to Volusia-Brevard County Line 0-20 nm

properties.description:

Twin Lakes, Hopewell, Aucilla, Cherry Lake, Hamburg, Pinetta,

properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued July 26 at 1:28PM EDT until July 26 at 2:30PM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
SMWCHS

The National Weather Service in Charleston has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from South Santee River to Edisto Beach SC out 20
NM...

* Until 230 PM EDT.

* At 128 PM EDT, severe thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts were located along a line from over Capers Island Buoy
to over Charleston Sixty, moving southeast at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to 40 knots.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Capers Reef, Rattlesnake Shoal, Charleston Nearshore Reef, Joe
Shuford Reef, Bull Breakers, Capers Island Buoy, Charleston Sixty,
Air Force Reef and Charleston Coastal Anglers.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Boaters should seek safe harbor immediately until these storms pass.
Wind gusts 34 knots or greater, high waves, dangerous lightning, and
heavy rain are possible with these storms.
properties.area: Coastal waters from South Santee River to Edisto Beach SC out 20 NM

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued July 26 at 1:17PM EDT until July 26 at 4:15PM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
FFWCHS

The National Weather Service in Charleston has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Charleston County in southeastern South Carolina...

* Until 415 PM EDT.

* At 117 PM EDT, Trained storm spotter reports heavy rainfall
producing flash flooding in Old Village, with 3 to 4 inches of
water moving over the roadways. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain have
fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 2 to 3 inches in 1 hour.
Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Trained spotters reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mount Pleasant, Isle Of Palms, Sullivan's Island, Mount Pleasant
Towne Centre, Boone Hall Plantation, Sullivans Island, Seaside
Farms, East Cooper Regional Medical Center and Snowden.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

moving east at 10 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts of 45 to 50 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Homestead, Coral Gables, Homestead Miami Speedway, Black Point, The
Redland, Kendall, Pinecrest, Florida City, Homestead Base, Naranja,
Princeton, Leisure City, Palmetto Bay, Cutler Bay, Zoo Miami, Goulds,
West Perrine, Homestead Bayfront Park, Richmond Heights, and South
Miami Heights.
properties.instruction:
These winds can down small tree limbs and branches, and blow around
unsecured small objects. Seek shelter in a safe building until the
storm passes.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued July 26 at 9:41AM EDT until July 26 at 2:45PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is ongoing.

* WHERE...A portion of eastern North Carolina, including the
following county, Dare.

* WHEN...Until 245 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 933 AM EDT, local law enforcement reported that portions
of NC12 remain underwater this morning with Dare County
Communications center reporting 4-5" across the roadway near
Pea Island. Overflowing poor drainage areas have already
caused minor flooding in the advisory area.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
the vicinity of Pea Island National Wildlife Refuge
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction: Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued July 26 at 8:31AM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

Nueces River At Cotulla affecting La Salle County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Three Rivers.

* WHEN...From Tuesday evening until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 40.0 feet, Significant flooding reaches miles from the
main channel, flooding homes in the flood plain near Three Rivers
to Lake Corpus Christi. Up to 4 feet of water is in River Creek
Acres Subdivision, flooding several homes. Kellner Camp along
County Road 336 floods, with water several feet deep surrounding
homes. Antelope Lane is flooded cutting off access to J.I. Hailey
Subdivision at Jones River bend. Water approaches the base of homes
along the river in Buckeye Knoll Subdivision, 2 miles west of
Swinny Switch.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 AM CDT Sunday the stage was 3.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 20.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
Tuesday evening and continue rising to 40.4 feet Friday morning.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 40.6
feet on 07/11/2007.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Air Quality Alert issued July 24 at 4:56PM MDT by NWS Missoula MT
properties.description:
AQAMSO

* WHAT...Air Quality Advisory due to smoke from wildfires.

Air Quality Index ranging from Moderate to Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups.

* WHERE...All Areas on the Nez Perce Reservation.

* WHEN...Until 10:00 AM PDT Monday July 27.

* IMPACTS...Those who experience health effects from smoke include
children under 18, elders, pregnant women, people with asthma
or have difficulty breathing, diabetes, heart problems or
otherwise compromised health, and people who have high exposure
(those who work, exercise, or spend extensive time outdoors).
properties.instruction:
Under the most severe pollution level, sensitive groups should avoid
outdoor exposure and limit indoor activities, and everyone should
restrict their outdoor activities.

Idaho Department of Health and Welfare
https://healthandwelfare.idaho.gov/health-wellness/environmental-
health/wildfire-smoke
Idaho Smoke Information Hotline: 1-800-345-1007
